description: Native Windows hooks post every event to appa-runtime through PowerShell. hook.ps1 protects only sessions launched with APPA_GATE=1 (the clappa function); without the variable it exits 0 and -SessionContext prints nothing; appa init claude-code installs the runtime before it registers this plugin. In a protected session hook.ps1 blocks prompt and tool authorization failures and returns a structured block when a successful tool result cannot be admitted. SessionStart first starts the installed runtime when nothing healthy answers /health. The hook deadline outlasts the runtime's own 120-second evidence deadline. SessionStart also prints session-context.md as non-enforcing guidance. UserPromptSubmit refuses every prompt while a subagent definition in the project or user agents directory or an installed plugin declares maxTurns: Claude Code ends such a subagent at its cap with no SubagentStop, so its partial output would reach the parent unchecked. SubagentStart prints the runtime's context for the subagent (what its return must look like, when the parent declared a shape or a sanitizer), which Claude Code adds to the subagent's context. SubagentStop is the subagent's return check: the runtime checks the subagent's final message there and answers a block when that message may not cross, with the reason or with the exact text a sanitizer made of it, which keeps the subagent running until it stops with one that may, so hook.ps1 blocks there like a tool hook. Stop and StopFailure are the exception to the blocking exit: they report the root actor's finished turn, which decides nothing, and blocking there holds the actor in a turn it has already finished, so hook.ps1 exits 0 for them and takes the shorter deadline. The runtime closes on that event a call the harness never ran: a call refused at its permission prompt fires no outcome hook, and left open it would refuse every later call as a second one in flight.
